title: Exact Matrix Multiplication Exponent ω = 9/4 Over Every Field (Claimed Proof & Lean)
whyItMatters: Claims to settle the 57-year quest since Strassen (1969) by proving ω = 9/4 = 2.25 exactly over every field—simultaneously slashing the upper bound from 2.371 and refuting the famous ω = 2 conjecture.
summary: Building on its October 2 upper bound (ω ≤ 9/4, independently exposed by Amir Shpilka at ECCC and extended over arbitrary fields by Amanov, van den Berg, and Zuiddam), OpenAI released a 111-page November 24 preprint via its Euclidean tensor geometry framework claiming the matching lower bound ω ≥ 9/4 over every field. Corollary 1.2 asserts every n × n formal arithmetic circuit needs at least ⌈n^(9/4)/2⌉ multiplication or division gates, pinning the asymptotic rank of matrix multiplication to n^(9/4).
technicalHighlights: Pairs the verified ω ≤ 9/4 upper bound (far below the prior 2.371177 record) with a new matching lower bound ω ≥ 9/4 via Euclidean geometry in the asymptotic spectrum of tensors.
Accompanied by a Lean 4 formalization (ExactExponent.lean) proving the exact square exponent 9/4 for division-free circuits over every field.
Part of OpenAI’s November 24 family 379 release spanning seven interconnected tensor-geometry and complexity manuscripts.
caveats: Unreviewed preprint released November 24, 2026. Notably, the accompanying Lean 4 formalization is narrower than the full manuscript—covering division-free formal polynomial circuits rather than arbitrary circuits with division—so the general lower bound still awaits full human specialist refereeing.
contributors: Amir Shpilka & Jeroen Zuiddam et al. (Upper-Bound Expositions)
institutions: Tel Aviv University & University of Amsterdam (Upper-Bound Checks)

scoreRationale.foundational: If fully verified, pinning down the exact matrix multiplication exponent ω = 9/4 resolves one of the crown-jewel open problems in theoretical computer science.
scoreRationale.ripple: Reshapes algebraic complexity, tensor rank theory, and every algorithm whose runtime is parameterized by ω.
scoreRationale.verification: Upper bound already has independent human expositions and Lean checks division-free circuits, but the full Nov 24 lower bound remains unreviewed.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed decades of incremental ~0.0001 improvements into a single leap to 2.25 plus matching lower bound within two months.
